description: A 2-bedroom house inspired by the traditional Filipino Bahay Kubo stilt house, blending indigenous design principles with modern livability. Features raised flooring, steep thatched-style roofing, open-plan living, and natural cross-ventilation throughout.

architectural_style.era: Contemporary adaptation of pre-colonial Filipino vernacular architecture
architectural_style.philosophy: Harmony with tropical environment, community-oriented living, sustainable materials

site.orientation: Long axis east-west to minimize solar heat gain on walls
site.foundation: Concrete stilts with wooden post caps

materials.structural_frame: Treated bamboo poles and Philippine hardwood (Molave) posts
materials.walls: Woven bamboo slat panels (amakan) with sliding capiz shell windows
materials.flooring: Split bamboo slats over hardwood joists
materials.roof: Nipa palm thatch layered over bamboo purlins, with concealed waterproof membrane
materials.foundation_stilts: Reinforced concrete piers with hardwood post connections

rooms.name: Covered Porch (Batalan)
rooms.description: Traditional wide porch with bamboo bench seating, the social heart of the home. Features a bamboo railing and overhanging roof eave for rain protection.

rooms.name: Living & Dining Area (Sala)
rooms.description: Open-plan communal space with high vaulted ceiling following the steep roof line. Woven bamboo walls with large capiz shell sliding windows on all sides for maximum airflow.
features: Capiz shell sliding windows on 3 walls

rooms.name: Kitchen (Kusina)
rooms.description: Semi-open kitchen positioned at the back of the house per Bahay Kubo tradition, with a pass-through window to the rear garden. Modern appliances integrated into bamboo cabinetry.
features: Open shelving with woven basket storage

rooms.name: Bedroom 1 (Master - Silid Tulugan)
rooms.description: Primary bedroom with woven bamboo accent wall, capiz shell windows with wooden shutters for privacy, and a built-in bamboo wardrobe.
features: Capiz shell windows with hardwood shutters

rooms.name: Bedroom 2 (Silid Tulugan)
rooms.description: Second bedroom with similar Bukito detailing. Slightly smaller but with the same natural ventilation and material palette.
features: Capiz shell windows with hardwood shutters

rooms.name: Bathroom (Banyo)
rooms.description: Modern bathroom with river stone flooring, rainwater shower, and natural ventilation via high bamboo lattice panel.

rooms.name: Under-house Storage (Silong)
rooms.description: Traditional Bahay Kubo under-house space created by the stilts. Used for storage, livestock area, or shaded gathering space. Concrete pad with drainage.

floor_plan.circulation: Central hallway connecting sala to bedrooms and bathroom, with the kitchen accessed directly from the sala.

ventilation.details: Capiz shell sliding windows on all exterior walls, bamboo lattice panels above interior walls, high peaked roof creates stack effect drawing hot air upward and out through ridge vents.

roof.material: Layered nipa palm thatch over waterproof membrane
roof.details: Deep eaves protect walls from rain and provide shade. Ridge vent allows hot air to escape.

stairs.details: Traditional wide steps with bamboo railings, removable for security (historic feature).

sustainability.materials: 95% locally sourced and renewable (bamboo, nipa, hardwood)
sustainability.energy: Passive cooling eliminates need for air conditioning in most conditions
sustainability.water: Roof rainwater collection into ground-level cistern

structural_notes.seismic_resilience: Lightweight bamboo frame with flexible joints absorbs earthquake forces, following centuries-old Filipino building wisdom.
structural_notes.typhoon_resistance: Steep roof pitch and deep eaves reduce wind uplift. Flexible bamboo frame sways rather than snaps. Nipa thatch secured with bamboo battens and rope lashing.
structural_notes.flood_protection: 1.5m elevation on stilts keeps living space above typical flood levels.
structural_notes.termite_protection: Concrete stilts with metal caps prevent ground-to-wood termite access. Treated bamboo and hardwood throughout.

estimated_costs.note: Approximately PHP 740,000 (~USD 13,200). Costs vary by region and material availability.
